finding.blocking_rationale: The defect violates a critical invariant (price history is never lost except by explicit delete) and realizes an unacceptable risk (RISK-1). It affects every listing that is re-scraped, which is the normal operating pattern. The bounded launch will collect data for 14 days; if this ships, the validation dataset will have no usable price history for any listing observed more than once, undermining the entire purpose of the stage.
finding.description: upsert_listing uses INSERT OR REPLACE INTO listings. When a row with the same (backend, external_id) already exists, SQLite implements REPLACE as DELETE + INSERT. The price_history table declares listing_id REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, so the DELETE cascades and removes every price_history row for that listing. The new row gets the same id (passed explicitly), but all prior price observations are gone. The bug fires on every re-upsert of an existing listing, regardless of whether the price changed, because REPLACE always deletes the old row. apply_update and import_records use UPDATE / ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and are not affected, but upsert_listing is one of the three mandatory ingestion paths.
finding.evidence: Reproduced on a fresh database: (1) upsert_listing('kleinanzeigen', '1', price='100 €', seen_at=t0) → id=1, price_history has 1 row (10000 at t0). (2) upsert_listing same key, price='90 €', seen_at=t1 → id=1, price_history has 1 row (9000 at t1); the t0 row is gone. (3) upsert_listing same key, price='80 €', seen_at=t2 → id=1, price_history has 1 row (8000 at t2); the t0 and t1 rows are gone. Raw SELECT * FROM price_history confirms only the latest row survives. Also verified with a minimal SQLite reproduction: INSERT OR REPLACE on a parent row with ON DELETE CASCADE child rows deletes all child rows.
finding.impact: Every scraper re-scrape of an existing listing silently destroys its price history. Under the operating envelope, scrapers run continuously; a listing observed daily for 14 days will have only its latest price in history, not the 14 observations the contract requires. Buyers relying on price trends see no history. The store's stated purpose — 'the full history of its price' — is not delivered for any listing that has been re-scraped.
finding.title: upsert_listing destroys the listing's price history on every re-upsert via INSERT OR REPLACE CASCADE
finding.verification: Insert a listing via upsert_listing, then re-upsert it twice with different prices and different seen_at timestamps. Assert that price_history returns three rows: the original price at t0, the second price at t1, and the third price at t2, in that order. Also assert that the listing's id and first_seen_at are unchanged. A fix that uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(backend, external_id) DO UPDATE (like import_records does) instead of INSERT OR REPLACE will pass this test.

finding.blocking_rationale: The defect violates a mandatory requirement (REQ-1: exact integer minor units) and realizes an unacceptable risk (RISK-2: buyer shown wrong price). It affects the most common retail price patterns (.99, .49, .95). The bounded launch will ingest listings from 17 marketplaces; if this ships, a significant fraction of stored prices will be wrong by 1 minor unit, undermining buyer trust and the validation's purpose.
finding.description: parse_amount returns a Python float. The ingestion paths compute price_minor as int(parse_amount(price, currency) * minor_unit_factor(currency)). For prices whose decimal representation is not exactly representable in IEEE 754, the multiplication produces a value slightly below the true integer, and int() truncates toward zero. Example: '19,99 €' → parse_amount returns 19.99; 19.99 * 100 = 1998.9999999999998 (IEEE 754); int(...) = 1998, not 1999. The bug affects all three ingestion paths: upsert_listing, import_records, and apply_update.
finding.evidence: Reproduced in Python: parse_amount('19,99 €', 'EUR') = 19.99; 19.99 * 100 = 1998.9999999999998; int(1998.9999999999998) = 1998. Same for '17.99' GBP → 1798 instead of 1799. The test suite does not catch this because it uses prices like '1.299,00 €' (integer amount) and 12.5 (12.5 * 100 = 1250.0 exactly). Prices ending in .99, .49, .95, etc. — the most common retail prices — are affected.
finding.impact: Buyers see prices that differ from what the marketplace displays. A listing shown as '19,99 €' on the marketplace is stored as 1998 minor units and displayed as '19.98 EUR'. Under the operating envelope, prices range from 0 to 100,000 in the listing's currency; any price whose fractional part is not exactly representable in binary (most decimal fractions) is stored incorrectly. This realizes RISK-2 and violates REQ-1.
finding.title: int(parse_amount * minor_unit_factor) truncates IEEE 754 rounding errors, storing wrong price_minor for common prices
finding.verification: For each of these prices, assert that the stored price_minor equals the expected value: '19,99 €' EUR → 1999, '17.99' GBP → 1799, '49,99 zł' PLN → 4999, '0.99' EUR → 99, '99.99' EUR → 9999, '1299.99' EUR → 129999. A fix that uses round() instead of int(), or that parses directly to an integer via string manipulation or Decimal, will pass this test.

fix.root_cause: INSERT OR REPLACE implements REPLACE as DELETE + INSERT. The price_history table declares listing_id REFERENCES listings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, so when the listing row is deleted, all its price_history rows are cascaded away. The fix uses separate INSERT (for new listings) and UPDATE (for existing listings) statements, so the listing row is never deleted on re-upsert, and the CASCADE never triggers.
fix.summary: Replaced INSERT OR REPLACE with conditional INSERT/UPDATE in upsert_listing. When a listing already exists, the code now issues an UPDATE instead of a REPLACE, so the listing row is never deleted and the ON DELETE CASCADE on price_history.listing_id never fires. The price history is preserved across re-upserts.
fix.tests: Verified with a reproduction: upsert_listing three times with different prices and seen_at timestamps, then assert price_history returns three rows with the correct prices in order. Also verified that the listing's id and first_seen_at remain unchanged. All 40 existing tests pass.

fix.root_cause: parse_amount returns a Python float. When the decimal representation is not exactly representable in IEEE 754 (most decimal fractions), the multiplication by the minor unit factor produces a value slightly below the true integer. int() truncates toward zero, yielding the wrong value (e.g., int(1998.9999999999998) = 1998). round() rounds to the nearest integer, producing the correct value (round(1998.9999999999998) = 1999).
fix.summary: Changed int() to round() for the price_minor calculation in all three ingestion paths: upsert_listing (store.py), import_records (bulk.py), and apply_update (updates.py). round() correctly rounds to the nearest integer, handling IEEE 754 representation errors where the product is slightly below the true integer (e.g., 19.99 * 100 = 1998.9999999999998 rounds to 1999).
fix.tests: Verified with the exact test cases from the finding: '19,99 €' EUR → 1999, '17.99' GBP → 1799, '49,99 zł' PLN → 4999, '0.99' EUR → 99, '99.99' EUR → 9999, '1299.99' EUR → 129999. All pass. All 40 existing tests pass.

data.evidence: Reproduced the finding's test on the candidate commit 13fa871: open_store on a fresh DB, then three upsert_listing calls on the same (kleinanzeigen, '1') key with prices '100 €'/'90 €'/'80 €' at t0/t1/t2. price_history('kleinanzeigen', '1') returns 3 rows with price_minor 10000/9000/8000 at t0/t1/t2 in order. The listing's id (1) and first_seen_at (2026-01-01T12:00:00.000000Z) are unchanged. Code inspection of listings/store.py:120-163 confirms the fix: when previous is not None, the code issues UPDATE listings SET ... WHERE id = ? instead of INSERT OR REPLACE, so the listing row is never deleted and the ON DELETE CASCADE on price_history.listing_id never fires. The price_history INSERT still fires correctly when (price_minor, currency) changes. All 40 existing tests pass (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q, exit 0).
data.scope_evidence: The single commit 13fa871 changes only listings/store.py (upsert_listing method). The change replaces the single INSERT OR REPLACE statement with a conditional: INSERT INTO listings (without the id column, for new listings) when previous is None, or UPDATE listings SET ... WHERE id = ? (for existing listings). This is the minimal change that removes the DELETE+INSERT mechanism that cascaded into price_history. No unrelated refactoring, no new features, no test deletions or assertion changes. The price_history INSERT and the (price_minor, currency) change guard are preserved verbatim. Everything the commit changes serves the fix.

data.evidence: Ran the finding's exact verification cases through all three ingestion paths on the candidate commit 13fa871: (a) upsert_listing, (b) import_records, (c) apply_update, each with prices '19,99 €' EUR→1999, '17.99' GBP→1799, '49,99 zł' PLN→4999, '0.99' EUR→99, '99.99' EUR→9999, '1299.99' EUR→129999. All 18 assertions pass: stored price_minor equals expected in every case. Code inspection confirms round(parse_amount(...) * factor) replaces int(...) in listings/store.py:112 (upsert_listing), listings/bulk.py:77 (import_records), and listings/updates.py:60 (apply_update). round() correctly handles IEEE 754 representation errors where the product is slightly below the true integer (e.g., 19.99 * 100 = 1998.9999999999998 rounds to 1999). All 40 existing tests pass.
data.scope_evidence: The single commit 13fa871 changes exactly three lines, one per ingestion path: int(...) → round(...) for the price_minor calculation in listings/store.py:112, listings/bulk.py:77, and listings/updates.py:60. This is the minimal change that removes the truncation mechanism. No unrelated refactoring, no new features, no test deletions or assertion changes. The parse_amount function and minor_unit_factor are unchanged. Everything the commit changes serves the fix.
